newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi to present detailed govt plans.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi to present detailed govt plans.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi will present the government's detailed policy plans in a keynote speech to the Senate (upper house) later on Thursday, Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said.

Government ally, the hard left Communist Refoundation, had asked Prodi not to commit the government to a precise programme in the speech, which will open the way for a vote of confidence in the centre-left administration at around 1930 GMT.
Dini, who heads the small centrist Italian Renewal party, had demanded that Prodi clearly spell out government plans, forcing Refoundation to back a precise programme.

Prodi unveiled the contents of his speech to ministers at a cabinet meeting ahead of the parliamentary debate. Dini told reporters after the meeting he was "satisfied" by the text, which will be used as the basis of the confidence motion.

"It is an all-comprehensive speech which will show what are the government's intentions and what will be its actions in the near-future," Dini said, adding there would be clear indications on plans to reform the Welfare State.

Prodi was forced to call the confidence debate after Refoundation, which secures his government's parliamentary majority, had refused to back plans to send a security force to Albania. A similar vote is set for the lower house on Saturday. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
